CheckTitle: GitLab runners do not execute jobs in privileged containers
Description: A GitLab runner using the Docker executor in **privileged mode** grants each CI job full capabilities on the host kernel. This check reports runners configured with `privileged = true`, which is commonly enabled to support Docker-in-Docker image builds.
Risk: A privileged container is not a security boundary: any job can mount the **host filesystem**, reach the Docker socket and read the build caches, registry credentials and job tokens of **every other project** that shares the runner. A single untrusted merge request pipeline therefore escalates to full compromise of the runner host and lateral access across tenants.

Code.CLI:
# Edit /etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml on the runner host:
#   [runners.docker]
#     privileged = false
sudo gitlab-runner restart
Code.Other:
1. Open `/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml` on the runner host
2. Under `[runners.docker]`, set `privileged = false`
3. Replace Docker-in-Docker image builds with a rootless builder such as Buildah, Kaniko or BuildKit in rootless mode
4. Restart the runner with `gitlab-runner restart`
5. Where privileged builds remain unavoidable, dedicate a single-tenant ephemeral runner to them and never share it with other projects
Code.Terraform:
# helm_release values for gitlab-runner
runners:
  privileged: false
  config: |
    [[runners]]
      [runners.kubernetes]
        privileged = false

Recommendation.Text: Disable privileged mode on shared runners and build images with a rootless builder such as Kaniko or Buildah. If a privileged runner is unavoidable, isolate it to a single trusted project on ephemeral infrastructure.
